_comment: Phase 6i. Something is in the dead-letter queue and nobody has dealt with
it. The other half of phase 6's last exit criterion.
WHY payorch.dlq.pending AND NOT payorch.dlq.records - THE WHOLE POINT
The phase plan says 'alerts on consumer lag and DLQ DEPTH', and depth is the
wrong number. A Kafka topic is a log: replaying a dead-lettered record moves
a consumer offset, it does not delete anything. So the record count rises
forever and never falls.
A rule thresholding it fires during the first incident and then STAYS FIRING
for the life of the cluster - which is worse than no rule, because it trains
a team to close the notification without reading it, and the second incident
arrives on a channel everybody has learned to ignore.
pending is end offset minus the REPLAY GROUP's committed offset. It returns
to zero when somebody replays or triages, which is the property an alert
actually needs and the one 'depth' does not have.
payorch.dlq.records is published too, and is deliberately not alerted on: 12
pending out of 12 records is a new incident, 12 out of 4,000 is a Tuesday,
and that ratio is what the person who gets paged wants in front of them.
matchType 1 is 'at least once', and here it is right where it is wrong for
consumer-lag. Lag is a rate problem - a spike that drains is healthy. A
dead-lettered payment is a discrete event: it has already exhausted 5s, 1m
and 10m of retries, so by the time it lands here it is not going to resolve
itself, and one is worth knowing about.
target 0 with op > for the same reason. There is no healthy non-zero level
of unhandled dead letters.
No alertOnAbsent, unlike consumer-lag. Absence here would fire on every
stack that runs without the async profile, which is phases 1 to 5 - and the
gauge that matters for 'is the consumer alive at all' is already the lag one.
Two rules alerting on the same silence is one rule and one snooze button.

annotations.description: Records are sitting in {{$labels.topic}} that the replay group has not consumed. Each one is a payment event that failed its first attempt and all three retry tiers. Inspect with GET /actuator/dlq?sample=5 and replay with POST /actuator/dlq once the cause is fixed.
